cefrAlignment: Matches B1 reading for orientation (CEFR CV: can skim short texts to find the gist and relevant facts on familiar topics): two 209- and 234-word texts on everyday topics with high-frequency vocabulary and simple linear paragraph structure, and tasks limited to gist, topic sentences and main idea versus detail.
examFidelity: Skills are relevant to IELTS Matching headings, TOEFL Read an Academic Passage and TOEIC Part 7 purpose questions; the TOEFL and TOEIC tips were softened so they no longer state question types that exams.ts does not list (TOEFL lists purpose and connection between ideas, not 'main idea').
fixes: Replaced an unattributed, unverifiable statistic ('In 2023, 40% of 25-year-olds still lived at home') with a clearly hedged survey example
Replaced the unverifiable claim that an electric drill is 'used for only a few minutes in its whole life' with a general statement, and updated the ex4 prompt and title distractor that quoted it
Corrected the ex2 q2 explanation: paragraph B describes how the system works, so the benefits are in C and D, not 'B–D'
Softened the TOEIC learn tip from 'Part 7 often starts with…' to 'often includes questions like…'
Rewrote the TOEFL exam tip to match the question types listed in exams.ts (writer's purpose, connection between ideas)
openConcerns: Rendering: the match component labels the right-hand options A, B, C… while the left side says 'Paragraph A', 'Paragraph B'. In ex3 this letter clash may confuse learners. It is a UI issue in src/components/exercises/MatchExercise.tsx, outside this file.
learnerOutcome: A learner can skim a 200–250-word everyday text in about two minutes, state its main idea, pick out topic sentences and separate main ideas from supporting details.
